nodes.name: Probe Auth Gate
nodes.notes: Shared-secret check for /webhook/infra-probe. Header X-Nexus-Probe-Key, or ?key= as a fallback. Dormant while $env.NEXUS_PROBE_KEY is unset. Always emits one item so the responseNode webhook can never hang; 'Probe Authorized?' does the routing.

nodes.name: Probe Authorized?
nodes.notes: TRUE -> run the probe. FALSE -> 'Respond Unauthorized' (HTTP 401). typeVersion 2.2 matches the IF nodes used elsewhere in this system.

nodes.name: Respond Unauthorized
nodes.notes: HTTP 401 with a body that says nothing about WAHA. Deliberately identical for a missing key and a wrong key.

nodes.name: Probe Passed?
nodes.notes: TRUE -> 'Respond' (200 PASS). FALSE -> 'Respond Degraded' (503 FAIL). Two fixed-code Respond nodes rather than one node with an expression in options.responseCode, because a fixed integer is certain to work and an expression there is not.

nodes.name: Respond Degraded
nodes.notes: HTTP 503 carrying the verdict and the reasons array. This is the whole point of the change: an uptime checker pointed at this URL now actually goes red when WhatsApp is down.

nodes.name: Every 15 Minutes
nodes.notes: Gives the probe a caller. 96 runs/day, each one small HTTP call inside the Docker network -- negligible on an e2-micro. saveDataSuccessExecution is 'none' for this workflow, so these runs do not accumulate in the database.

nodes.name: Probe Alarm
nodes.notes: Throws on a FAIL verdict so the configured error workflow (iYJkh1kztWxZXDbT) raises it. De-duplicated via $getWorkflowStaticData: alerts on the 1st consecutive failure and then every 8th (~2 hours). Positioned below and right of both Respond nodes so under executionOrder v1 the HTTP response is sent first.
